title: Intermittent fasting and neurodegenerative diseases: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic potential.
authors: Lv, Renjun; Liu, Bin; Jiang, Ziying; Zhou, Runfa; Liu, Xiaoxing; Lu, Tangsheng; Bao, Yanping; Huang, Chunxia; Zou, Guichang; Zhang, Zongyong; Lu, Lin; Yin, Qingqing
one_liner_zh: 综述间歇性禁食对神经退行性疾病的分子机制与治疗潜力，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders are straining public health worldwide. During neurodegenerative disease progression, aberrant neuronal network activity, bioenergetic impairment, adaptive neural plasticity impairment, dysregulation of neuronal Ca(2+) homeostasis, oxidative stress, and immune inflammation manifest as characteristic pathological changes in the cellular milieu of the brain. There is no drug for the treatment of neurodegenerative disorders, and therefore, strategies/treatments for the prevention or treatment of neurodegenerative disorders are urgently needed. Intermittent fasting (IF) is characterized as an eating pattern that alternates between periods of fasting and eating, requiring fasting durations that vary depending on the specific protocol implemented. During IF, depletion of liver glycogen stores leads to the production of ketone bodies from fatty acids derived from adipocytes, thereby inducing an altered metabolic state accompanied by cellular and molecular adaptive responses within neural networks in the brain. At the cellular level, adaptive responses can promote the generation of synapses and neurons. At the molecular level, IF triggers the activation of associated transcription factors, thereby eliciting the expression of protective proteins. Consequently, this regulatory process governs central and peripheral metabolism, oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial function, autophagy, and the gut microbiota, all of which contribute to the amelioration of neurodegenerative disorders. Emerging evidence suggests that weight regulation significantly contributes to the neuroprotective effects of IF. By alleviating obesity-related factors such as blood-brain barrier dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and beta-amyloid accumulation, IF enhances metabolic flexibility and insulin sensitivity, further supporting its potential in mitigating neurodegenerative disorders. The present review summarizes animal and human studies investigating the role and underlying mechanisms of IF in physiology and pathology, with an emphasis on its therapeutic potential. Furthermore, we provide an overview of the cellular and molecular mechanisms involved in regulating brain energy metabolism through IF, highlighting its potential applications in neurodegenerative disorders. Ultimately, our findings offer novel insights into the preventive and therapeutic applications of IF for neurodegenerative disorders.
abstract_zh: 神经退行性疾病正给全球公共卫生带来沉重负担。在神经退行性疾病进展过程中，异常神经元网络活动、生物能量损伤、适应性神经可塑性损伤、神经元Ca(2+)稳态失调、氧化应激及免疫炎症，表现为大脑细胞环境中特征性病理变化。目前尚无治疗神经退行性疾病的药物，因此亟需预防或治疗这些疾病的策略/疗法。间歇性禁食 (intermittent fasting, IF) 被定义为一种在禁食与进食周期之间交替的饮食模式，其禁食时长因具体实施方案而异。在IF期间，肝脏糖原储备的耗竭导致由脂肪细胞来源的脂肪酸生成酮体，从而诱导一种伴随大脑神经网内细胞和分子适应性反应的改变性代谢状态。在细胞水平上，适应性反应可促进突触和神经元的生成。在分子水平上，IF触发相关转录因子的激活，从而引发保护性蛋白的表达。因此，这一调控过程调节中枢和外周代谢、氧化应激、炎症、线粒体功能、自噬及肠道微生物群，所有这些均有助于改善神经退行性疾病。新兴证据表明，体重调节显著促进IF的神经保护作用。通过缓解肥胖相关因素，如血脑屏障功能障碍、神经炎症和β-淀粉样蛋白积累，IF增强代谢灵活性和胰岛素敏感性，进一步支持其在缓解神经退行性疾病方面的潜力。本综述总结了探讨IF在生理和病理中作用及其潜在机制的动物和人体研究，重点强调其治疗潜力。此外，我们概述了通过IF调节大脑能量代谢所涉及的细胞和分子机制，突出其在神经退行性疾病中的潜在应用。最终，我们的发现为IF在神经退行性疾病预防和治疗中的应用提供了新见解。
